content.text:
**My recommendation is short AI-written titles, like ChatGPT and Claude generally use, with the current text as a fallback.** They write a 3–6 word title in the background after the first message, the title just appears in the sidebar, and a manual rename always wins. I haven't changed any code yet.

Right now all three places show your raw words cut off, so they all start with the same "hey, can you tell me…":

| Place | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| **Sidebar, typed chat** | First 80 characters of the message (`app/api/chat/route.ts:74`, `components/chat-workspace.tsx:183`) | "Netto spending this month", generated while the answer streams |
| **Sidebar, call chat** | First thing you said (`app/api/chat/route.ts:74`, or `app/api/voice/calls/route.ts:23` if the call never asked anything) | Shows "Voice call" during the call, then gets a title like "Rent and grocery check" when it ends |
| **Task rows during a call** | Raw transcribed speech (`components/voice-call.tsx:81`) | Same short title, replacing the raw text a moment after the task starts |
| **Finished call card** | Raw task text under "Still running when the call ended" (`components/voice-call-card.tsx:33`) | Same short title |

**How it would work**
- **One helper:** a single function turns text into a title of 2–5 words, in your language. It uses a lighter model (`gpt-6-luna`, already used for imports) and is told not to include amounts it wasn't given.
- **Calls:** the call summary already makes an AI request, so it can return the title too, with no extra request. A call inside an existing chat keeps that chat's title.
- **Renames are safe:** the title is only replaced if it still matches the placeholder, so your renames stick and no database migration is needed.
- **If the AI fails:** typed chats keep today's text and call chats stay "Voice call". Task rows keep the spoken text.
- **Raw speech is kept:** the agent still gets your exact words, and "Requests from this call" and the transcript still show them.
- **Cost and privacy:** that's one small extra AI request per new chat and per call task, sent only to the AI provider you already set up.

**Decision for you: should I retitle your old chats too?**
I'd do it, because that's what you're seeing in the sidebar now. It would be a one-time background run that only touches chats whose title still matches their first message, so anything you renamed stays as it is. The first messages stay in the chat, but it costs one small AI request per old chat, and new chats would look right without it.

Should I build this, including the old chats?

Links: [{"title":"gghfez's picture","url":"https://huggingface.co/gghfez/openwebui-title-generator-270m/blob/main/README.md"},{"title":"huggingface.co","url":"https://huggingface.co/spaces/adityagaharawar/open-webui/blob/main/backend/open_webui/routers/tasks.py"},{"title":"huggingface.co","url":"https://huggingface.co/spaces/katsukiai/h3-Latest/blob/main/backend/open_webui/routers/tasks.py"},{"title":"# Task Models","url":"https://docs.openwebui.com/features/administration/task-models.md"},{"title":"task models","url":"https://docs.openwebui.com/features/administration/task-models"},{"title":"docs.openwebui.com","url":"https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/essentials/"},{"title":"Which model is responsible for naming of the thread?","url":"https://huggingface.co/spaces/huggingchat/chat-ui/discussions/402"}]

Open WebUI generates chat titles with a background "task model," separate from the model answering you, and the search results describe the pieces below.

- **Task model:** Open WebUI makes small background calls for jobs like titles, tags, and follow-up suggestions. Which model it uses depends on the connection the chat model came from: a Local Task Model for local connections and an External Task Model for OpenAI-compatible providers. By default, both default to Current Model, so background work runs on the chat's own model.
- **Trigger:** Title generation is controlled by an admin toggle, ENABLE_TITLE_GENERATION. The docs also say that if a named task model is no longer available, background work falls back to the chat's model.
- **Code path:** A snippet of Open WebUI's `tasks.py` router (mirrored on Hugging Face, not the official repo) shows a `generate_title` endpoint. It checks whether title generation is enabled, strips reasoning blocks from messages, and fills a title prompt template with the chat messages. It then sends the result through `generate_chat_completion` with a token cap, with the task recorded as a title-generation job. The template is filled with the messages and user details such as name and location.
- **Prompt:** A community fine-tune's README shows the expected style of the title prompt: a short, 3–5 word title, often with an emoji, returned as JSON from the chat history. This is a third-party model card, so it describes the intended output rather than the built-in prompt text.
- **Practical tip:** The docs advise using a small, non-reasoning model for this. A title that comes back cut off is the usual symptom of a reasoning task model, because thinking tokens count against the same token budget.

I did not find the exact default title prompt text in these results. The official task-models page at docs.openwebui.com covers the settings and the prompt-editing section, which is the best place to check the current defaults.

# Thread titles

Generates thread titles for real thread shapes with the server's Codex title generator, then sets each new title against the old one for a blind review.

## Run

```sh
cd evals
pnpm thread-titles --model <codex model> --out runs/titles
pnpm thread-titles --model <codex model> --out runs/titles-new --baseline runs/titles/results.json
```

- It uses your local Codex login, like the server does.
- `--initial` titles from the first message only, as a new thread does.
- A run writes `results.json` (titles and latency), `review.json` (titles A and B in random order, with a rubric), and `answer-key.json`. Score `review.json` before you open `answer-key.json`.

## Add a case

Add an entry to `cases.ts` with an `id`, a `source`, the thread `messages`, the `previousTitle`, and a `rubric` that says what a good title names.

content.text:
**There isn't a better way: T3 Code and the open-source apps I checked all make one small AI request to write the title.** That's also the easy way, because the helper is only a few lines. Most of the work is showing the title in the sidebar and on call tasks.

| App | How it titles a chat | If that fails or the model is missing |
|---|---|---|
| **T3 Code** | Uses the first message for a new thread, and the thread contents plus the old title for **Regenerate title** | Not checked |
| **OpenHands** | Sends the first message, cut to 1,000 characters | First 30 characters of the message |
| **Crush** | Sends the first message to its configured "small" model, with an 80-character limit | Not checked |
| **Open WebUI** | Uses a separate background "task model", and its docs advise a small one | Falls back to the chat's own model |

ChatGPT and Claude are closed source, so what I said about them earlier comes from how they behave, not from their code.

**Other options I'd skip**
- **No AI, just cleaning the text:** removing "hey, can you…" means keeping word lists for English and German, and you still get long fragments rather than titles.
- **Having the answering model write the title:** the title would wait for the full answer, and we'd have to separate it out of the reply.
- **Having the voice model name call tasks:** its handoff carries no text, which is why tasks use your transcribed speech today (`lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts:183`).

**Worth copying from T3 Code**
- **Vague first messages:** the model also returns `needsRefinement` when the subject is still unknown, such as "fix this". We could use that for "hey" or "can you help me", then retitle after your next message. This matters for us because people often open with a greeting. I only saw the flag, not how T3 Code acts on it.
- **Regenerate title:** a menu item next to Rename and Delete is a small addition and gives you a fix for a bad title.

My plan stays the same, with those two added. Should I build it, including retitling your old chats?
